messages.author: caaac2dc0aae28b8
messages.subject: high %CV in bootstrap abundance estimates
parts:
I=92m doing an analysis of some line transect data with several strata, u=
sing=20
MCDS to estimate detection functions using all the data, and then produci=
ng=20
stratum-specific abundance estimates. I used a bootstrap for variance=20=

estimates (n=3D2000), and I used a size-bias regression for estimating cl=
uster=20
size within strata (logE(s) on g(x)). For 2 of the strata, I=92m getting=
some=20
really large bootstrap variance estimates (%CV>100). From the bootstrap=20=

results file, I see that I have a few large E(s) within these strata, and=
I=20
suspect this is due to pulling some very sparse data within these strata =
for a=20
few of the bootstrap replicates, which result in wacky regression equatio=
ns. I=20
want to report the %CV along with the bootstrap group size, abundance and=
=20
density estimates. Do these large %CVs really reflect the bootstrap resu=
lts,=20
or should I remove these =93outliers=94 and recalculate the bootstrap var=

iance and=20
%CV from the remaining replicates?

--

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: high %CV in bootstrap abundance estimates
parts:
Eric, if it is reasonable to assume that all strata have the same E(s),=20
that might be your best option. If not, but you don't have much=20
evidence of size bias, you can estimate E(s) by the sample mean of=20
cluster size in each stratum. If neither of these is a reasonable=20
option, I might resort to dropping the bootstrap estimates for which the=20
bias-adjusted E(s) is clearly implausible, and report the % discarded.

Steve
